historical_context: The Taj Mahal was commissioned in 1632 by the Mughal emperor Shah Jahan to house the tomb of his favorite wife, Mumtaz Mahal. It was completed in 1648, with the surrounding gardens and buildings finished shortly thereafter. It is a UNESCO World Heritage site representing the pinnacle of Mughal architecture.
verified_facts: The Taj Mahal is located in Agra, India.
It is built primarily of white marble.
It was designated a UNESCO World Heritage Site in 1983.
reasoning: The visual data (geometry, structural elements, iconic layout) matches historical and architectural records of the Taj Mahal. The lighting and perspective are consistent with standard photography of the site.
additional_observations: The reflection in the pool appears accurate and continuous with the physical architecture, indicating no digital manipulation of the building itself.
